URL: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-21/kazakhstan-to-stop-piping-oil-to-black-sea-after-tanker-attacks
NOTE: Bloomberg (approved, snippet-only), Tue 21 Jul. Kazakhstan forced to SUSPEND crude shipments to its main Black Sea export terminal — the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) terminal near Russia's Novorossiysk — due to security concerns after a series of drone attacks on tankers; the terminal set to stop accepting piped supplies "because tanker companies are too nervous to send their ships." CPC handles ~80% of Kazakhstan's crude exports; producers face output cuts if suspension holds to week's end. Attacks (Ukrainian, unclaimed) hit tankers loading Kazakh third-party crude: 17 Jul Nordic Zenith damaged; 19 Jul Asia (Liberia-flag/Greek-owned) + Nissos Ios (Marshall Is/Greek-owned) set afire; 20 Jul Nelsa (156,000 dwt) set afire at SPM-1. Comes amid near-total Hormuz halt + Houthi Red Sea threat = compounding global oil-supply squeeze. Cross-ref: Russia FM spokeswoman Zakharova (Mon) condemned Ukraine drone strikes on CPC vessels as "terrorist attack against civilian infrastructure"; Kazakhstan FM called strikes unacceptable. Ukraine has not claimed responsibility.
